3. The defendant Nos. 1-12 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia, that the suit is barred by limitation; bad for defect of parties and not maintainable in its present form. Further case of the defendants are that the suit property originally belonged to one Ansar Ali and the same along with other property was sold in auction on 25-3-1934 for arrear rents in Execution Case No. 2893 of 1936. In the said auction the properly was purchased by the decree-holder Abdul Hamid Khondakar and others. Thereafter, said Abdul Hamid Khondakar and others settled die property to Zuma Gaji, Siraj Mia and Ibrahim who executed and registered two separate kabuliyatnama in favour of Abdul Hamid Khondakar and others on 4-2-1942. Said Zuma Gaji died leaving defendant No. 1 who got 37 decimals of land in plot No. 762. SA khatian accordingly stands recorded in his name to the extent of 8 annas share and also in the name of Ibrahim Mia and Siraj Mia to the extent of 4 annas each. Subsequent DP khatian also stand recorded in their names. The defendants have been possessing the suit property by way of inheritance and by settlement from 1942. The plaintiff has no right, title and possession in the suit property, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 6. Mr Sagir Anwar with Mr Gazi Md Mohsin, learned Advocates appearing for the petitioners submit that admittedly the property in question originally belonged to Ansar Ali. On die death of said Ansar Ali the property in question ultimately devolved upon Taherun Bibi as only heir. The dispute between contesting defendants is only in respect of plot No. 762 under CS khatian No. 4. The defendant Nos. 1-18 claim that the property covered by plot No. 762 was sold in auction in decree Execution Case Nos. 909 and 910 of 1938 on 25-3-1939 and the same was purchased by decree holder Abdul Hamid Khondaker and others. The said decree-holder, auction purchasers settled the property to Zuma Gaji, Ibrahim and Siraj Mia for which they executed and registered two separate kabuliyat deeds in favour of Abdul Hamid Khondakar and others on 24-2-1942 and 25-2-1942. The trial court as well as the appellate court concurrently found that the defendants could not produce any paper in support of auction sale of the property by producing any such proceedings and on that findings the trial court decreed the suit in preliminary form, but the appellate court though agreed with the findings and observations of the trial court that the defendants failed to submit any document regarding auction sale but held that the kabuliyat registered in the year 1942 is of 30 years old document. 

 7. Mr Sagir Anwar further submits that in any settlement by zaminder, documents must He executed by lessor and lessee both but in the instant suit the kabuliyat in question tire unilateral documents. As such, by the said kabuliyat the defendants did not acquire any title in the property. In support of his such contention he has referred to the case of Wazed Ali Sheikh vs Most Hazera Khatoon reported in 2008 BLD 215 and Md Nizamuddin vs Government of Bangladesh reported in 1985 BLD (AD) 235. He further submits that the defendants could not file any deed of settlement in their favour even a piece of rent receipt showing payment of rent by them to the zaminder at any point of time. As such, the settlement so far claimed by the defendants have got no basis at all. Further, he submits that the present: BS khatian also stands recorded in the name of the plaintiff pursuant to a decree passed in Land Survey Tribunal Case No. 1155 of 2013, It is also argued that the defendants could not substantiate their claim that the property of Ansar Ali was sold in auction in any proceedings by adducing any evidence both oral and documentary before the trial court. 

 8. Finally, he submits that the plaintiffs right from their predecessor Ansar Ali and then Taherun Bibi, continuously possessing the suit land, but the defendants all on a sudden claimed that the property acquired by them by kabuliyats of the year 1942 which never acted upon and show the day light. As such, the trial court rightly decreed the suit but the appellate court without considering evidences led by the plaintiffs on misconstruction of evidences and misconception of law allowed the appeal and dismissed the suit. He submits that while preparing himself for hearing of this revision found that the plaintiffs ought to have prayed for a declaration of their title in the property. But inadvertently it was omitted by the conducting lawyer for the petitioners for which the petitioners filed an application for amendment of the plaint, only to the extent of prayer portion and prays for allowing the application and to pass necessary order in this regard. 

 9. Mr Md Abdul Kader Bhuiyan, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties submits that in the recital of kabuliyat dated 24-2-1942 and 25-2-1942, it has been clearly mentioned that the property was auction purchased by Abdul Hamid Khondakar and others in Decree Execution Case No. 909 and 910 of the year 1938 and the suit property under plot No. 762 was settled by decree-holder auction-purchasers, Abdul Hamid Khondakar and others in favour of Zuma Gaji, Ibrahim and Siraj Mia who executed and registered two separate kabuliyatnama in favour of auction purchasers. Since then Zuma Gaji, thereafter, his heirs, Ibrahim and Siraj Mia have been possessing the suit land. Accordingly, SA khatian stand recorded in their names. Subsequently, DP khatian also stand recorded in the name of defendants which proves that said kabuliyat has been acted upon. After SAT Act came into force and abolition of zamindary system the government accepted the defendants and recognized them as tenants under the government. As such, the auction sale has been established and the auction purchaser settled the properly in favour of Zuma Gaji, Ibrahim and Siraj Mia has been proved. 

 12. Finally, he submits that kabuliyat of the year 1942, subsequent SA khatian and DP khatian in the name of defendants amply established that the property in question was sold in auction and decree-holder auction purchaser, Abdul Hamid Khondakar and others subsequently, settled the properly in favour of Zuma Gaji, Ibrahim and Siraj Mia for which they executed two separate kabuliyatnama in favour of auction purchasers. All those documents established that the defendant-opposite party acquired indefeasible right, title and interest in the properly and they have been possessing the same since 1942. As such, the appellate court rightly allowed the appeal and dismissed the suit. In support of his such contention he has referred to the case of Nurul Hoq Bhuiyan vs Momtazul Islam reported in 67 DLR (AD) 51 and Md Nizamuddin vs Government of Bangladesh reported in 1985 BLD (AD) 233. 

 14. It is admitted by both the parties that the property covered by plot No. 762 measuring 74 sataks recorded in the name of Ansar Ali in CS khatian No. 4. The plaintiff in suit claims that on the death of Ansar Ali and his son Kala Mia, Afsaruddin and daughter Karpurer Nessa, ultimately, the property devolved upon one Taherun Bibi. Said Taherun Bibi while in possession and enjoyment of the properly, she transferred 7 sataks of land to one Sufia Khatun Bibi by a registered deed timed 20-8-1949 with whom Taherun Bibi was in ejmali possession in the same plot. Said Sufia Khatun Bibi is defendant No. IS in the suit. It is also claimed by the plaintiffs that the property in question never sold in any auction and no notice was served upon their predecessor and there is no existence of such soil and execution case in the name of Ansar Ali or Taherun Bibi. Therefore, it is the obligation of the defendants to prove that the property covered by plot No. 762 was sold in auction in any decree execution case. The trial court as well as the appellate court held that the defendants though claim that the property was auction purchased by decree-holder Abdul Hamid Khondakar and others but could not produce any such proceedings before the court. But considering age of the registered kabuliyat, the appellate court held that the kabuliyat of the year 1942 are old registered deeds, as such, is admissible in evidence without any formal proof. 

 15. Both the parties to the proceeding, on candid, submit that there are some loopholes on the part of both the parties in conducting the suit. Learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that admittedly in plot No. 762 the defendants and the plaintiffs are not co-sharer, but in plot No. 772 the defendant No. 18 and the plaintiffs are co-sharers. Therefore, the suit for partition can only be maintained against the defendant No. 1.8 not against the defendant Nos. 1-17. It is also submitted that the plaintiffs ought to have prayed for declaration of title at least in respect of plot No. 762 which is claimed by the defendants by virtue of kabuliyat of the year 1942 and settlement in their favour by the owners Abdul Hamid Khondakar and others. In the situation, this Court finds that the plaint in suit has not been property framed seeking appropriate reliefs. Similarly, the defendants in suit admitted that the suit register of concern proceedings in which the property was sold in auction ought to have been filed before the trial court by the defendant. But they failed to do so, but filed a photocopy of certified copy of the register before the appellate court which was not properly presented by filing an application for taking additional evidence. 

 17. This Court also finds that both the parties did not file any rent receipts showing payment of rent to zaminder or to the government at any point of time. Only two kabuliyat has been filed by the defendants which are unilateral document and executed by them. Both the courts below remained silent on the points; whether by such kabuliyat the defendants acquired any title in the absence of any rent receipts showing payment of rent lo the lessor-zaminder or whether by a unilateral document of kabuliyat any tide passed in their favour. Therefore, this Court thinks it proper to send back the ease on remand to the trial court for fresh trial allowing both the parties to amend their pleadings suitably and to produce relevant document in support of their claim and adduce evidence if so advised.
